thread:
sarah-support: 🚨 Staging customers reporting 403 AFTER scheduled API key rotation window. Error payload says `insufficient_scope`. Only affects a subset of tenants (region=eu, prod-like config). Repro steps included below. Can eng take a look?

raj-eng: Thanks — can you paste the exact curl and response? Also which key was rotated (service vs consumer)?

sarah-support: curl we got from customer: ```curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_live_********\" https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/models/abc:generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'```
Response: `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden` JSON: `{\"error\":{\"code\":\"insufficient_scope\",\"message\":\"scope:models.generate required\"}}`
They say this worked before 03:00 UTC, fail after rotation. The rotated secret name: `staging/service-proxy/apikey/tenant-eu` (vault).

tim-ops: vault-bot shows a recent rewrap/rotate event for that path at 03:01 UTC. @vault-bot can you confirm KMS rewrap status and policy changes?

vault-bot: rotation event recorded: path=secret/data/staging/service-proxy/apikey/tenant-eu, operator=infra-rotations, rewrap_kms_key=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/prod-keys/cryptoKeys/rot-2026, new_version=3, metadata.tags=[\"service-proxy\",\"limited-scope\"]

raj-eng: metadata.tags includes `limited-scope` — that looks suspicious. Did the rotation job accidentally apply a policy-scoped wrapper that strips tenant-level scopes?

elaine-cs: Customer confirmed they saw a deployment hook that sanitized extra scopes: "applied minimal scopes for service accounts". They didn't expect scope trimming for this key.

tim-ops: Quick check: service-proxy caches auth metadata in memcached for 5m keyed by key-id header `x-api-key-id`. If the new key had the same id but new scope set, old cached entry might still be used — but that would show stale-permissions (old > new). Here we see reduction, so either cache contains new limited scope (unlikely) or the proxy is loading policy from a per-key policy service that returned trimmed scopes.

raj-eng: Repro locally: rotated a test key with `limited-scope` tag and proxied request returns 403 with same message. Looks like the policy-fetch layer (authz service) evaluates tags and applies a fallback minimal ACL when tag `limited-scope` present. This tag should never be added by the rotation job.

sarah-support: Customer asked if rollback is possible — they are blocked.

tim-ops: Steps to remediate (quick path): 1) Ask Vault team to rewrap with previous metadata (version=2) or remove `limited-scope` tag from new version. 2) Invalidate service-proxy auth cache: `memcached -e flush_all` on staging auth cluster or restart proxy pods if needed. 3) If any sidecars cache full policy, restart them too.

raj-eng: Longer-term: add an assertion in rotation job that tags don't mutate scope. Also add automated smoke test after rotation that runs a tenant-scoped auth check (`/internal/auth/check?scope=models.generate`). I can open a PR to add smoke check.

elaine-cs: For support response: apologized, offered temporary bypass (create short-lived key with full scope and rotate back), and provided ETA 45m for rollback. Customer accepted rollback.

tim-ops: I triggered a rollback to version=2 at 03:26 UTC and removed the `limited-scope` tag from new versions. Also flushed memcached on staging-auth-01 and restarted 2/3 proxy replicas to pick up policy.

raj-eng: Verified: requests for the tenant-eu key now return 200 for `models.generate` on my test harness.

elaine-cs: Customer confirmed services recovered at ~03:40 UTC. They want a postmortem and assurance this won't recur in prod.

tim-ops: Filed infra-tickets: INFRA-6721 (rotation-tag-safety), INFRA-6722 (post-rotation-smoke-check), and SUPPORT-4490 (customer incident). Leaving this thread for postmortem write-up. :white_check_mark:
